It allows developers to dynamically load, update, and run user-defined code at runtime. This article is the second part of the eBPF Tutorial by Example, focusing on using kprobe to capture the unlink system call in eBPF. The article will first explain the basic concepts and technical background of kprobes, and then introduce how to use kprobe to capture the unlink system call in eBPF. articles.title: 996 Isn't a Schedule. It's a Bargain Nobody Signed
articles.excerpt: In January 2021, a 22-year-old employee of the Chinese e-commerce company Pinduoduo died after leaving work at around 1:30 a.m. She collapsed on her way home. Her exact cause of death was never public…
articles.body: In January 2021, a 22-year-old employee of the Chinese e-commerce company Pinduoduo died after leaving work at around 1:30 a.m. She collapsed on her way home. Her exact cause of death was never publicly confirmed, and that uncertainty matters: it is precisely what turned a private tragedy into a public argument about how Chinese tech companies treat working time. The case did not become famous because of the death alone. It became famous because of what happened next. An account bearing Pinduoduo's name responded to questions about the death on Zhihu, a Chinese Q&A platform, with a message that essentially told readers that ordinary people survive by trading their health for money, and that this is simply the age we live in.

articles.title: The Elegance of Prevention: Why I Forced AI to Upgrade Its Problem-Solving Mindset
articles.excerpt: For the past week, I have been locked in a rigorous technical debate with ChatGPT. I was auditing the architecture for my project, GoChinaTrip, and our SSAP (Survival Semantic Action Protocol). What s…
articles.body: For the past week, I have been locked in a rigorous technical debate with ChatGPT. I was auditing the architecture for my project, GoChinaTrip, and our SSAP (Survival Semantic Action Protocol) . What started as a technical review escalated into a profound philosophical discussion about the fundamental difference between humans and AI. The revelation was this: When it comes to solving human problems, ChatGPT (and most modern AI) is playing a low-level game. Here is the reality. When a traveler encounters a digital deadlock in China—like their foreign Visa card failing at a restaurant for a 380 RMB bill—the standard AI response is to offer a "firefighting" fix at the exact moment of the crisis. It gives you a script to split the bill, or tells you what to say to the cashier.

articles.title: Healthtech Reminder Recovery: Why I Chose Delayed Jobs Before Cron
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use delayed queue messages for one-off user reminders due within seven days, and use cron to enqueue anything farther out or recurring. Keep the durable schedule in Postgres, make every…
articles.body: Short answer: use delayed queue messages for one-off user reminders due within seven days, and use cron to enqueue anything farther out or recurring. Keep the durable schedule in Postgres, make every send idempotent, and choose the queue or cron provider only after its region, retention, deletion, and processor boundaries pass your healthtech review. That split is my default because operational recovery matters more than shaving one component off the diagram. A reminder can be late without becoming wrong; a duplicate medication prompt can be much harder to explain. The database remains the source of truth, while the scheduling layer carries only a compact reminder ID.

The process exists, the container started, and a health endpoint answers. The process is healthy.

articles.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
articles.excerpt: Fast radio bursts are invisible, but a composer has turned thousands of them into sound at a Finnish cathedral, where a choir will sing along on Nov. 21.
articles.body: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 11, 1966: NASA launches Gemini 12 mission with astronaut icons Buzz Aldrin and Jim Lovell aboard
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program to land humans on the moon. Gemini 12 was the last mission of the Gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin . NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks. Before Gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Aldrin performed three spacewalks and spent more than five hours working in space with no major problems. Gemini 12 also successfully docked to an unpiloted Agena booster that launched the same day.

articles.body: Imagine you’ve crash-landed on an alien planet. Your ship is destroyed, your oxygen supply is dangerously low, and the landscape around you is completely unknown. This sci-fi thriller is written by acclaimed comic writer Benjamin Percy, executive produced by Andy Weir (Project Hail Mary, The Martian), and features an all-star voice cast including Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo . Stranded on an unfamiliar planet, they encounter volcanic wastelands, unknown skies, and environments that seem to defy reason.

articles.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
articles.excerpt: For over a century astronomers have speculated that comets could have delivered organic molecules necessary for life to Earth, but new modeling shows these molecules wouldn't have survived impact.
articles.body: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?

articles.title: 'There's tremendous demand': Rocket Lab raises price of Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab has raised the launch cost of its next-gen Neutron rocket by more than 25%, an increase that reflects high demand amid a looming liftoff bottleneck.
articles.body: The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground. Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027. "Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call.
